title: add control-plane VPC Terraform module: subnets, endpoints, SGs, peering, Route53 delegation
author: Aisha Rahman
description:
Motivation: Add a reusable Terraform module to provision the VPC and networking primitives required for the Redwood Private control plane. This PR bundles subnets (multi-AZ), NAT/GW placement guidance, interface and gateway endpoints for S3/Route53/EC2, security groups with minimal permissive rules, VPC peering support for customer VPCs, and Route53 delegated zone configuration.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds infra/terraform/modules/control-plane-vpc: module with variables, outputs, examples, and tests.
- Adds infra/terraform/live/{env}/control-plane/main.tf that consumes the module for prod/staging templates.
- Adds Route53 delegation helpers and optional private hosted zone creation (configurable).
- Introduces interface endpoints for SSM/EC2, gateway endpoints for S3, and route table configuration.
- Security groups are scoped to service IP ranges and support explicit inbound rules for healthchecks and kube bootstrap traffic.
- Supports optional cross-account VPC peering with acceptance toggles, and partial support for Transit Gateway via module variables (TGW attachment left as opt-in).

Requirements & compatibility:
- Compatible with terraform v1.4+ and AWS provider >= 4.50.0.
- Designed to be consumed by Redwood Private installer (helm + operator) to create control-plane networking in customer-managed AWS accounts.
- Backwards-compatible for existing live stacks: module exposes flags to adopt existing subnets, security groups, and hosted zones.

Testing performed:
- Ran terraform fmt/validate on modules and live stacks.
- End-to-end apply in a dedicated dev account (dev-cp-network) with 3 AZs: verified subnets, endpoints, and peering acceptance.
- Smoke test: control-plane instances boot and register with the private control plane operator in the deployed VPC.
- Manual Route53 delegation validation with a customer-simulated account.

Checklist (PR):
- [x] Module scaffold + examples
- [x] Variable and output documentation
- [x] Minimal default SG rules and opt-out for wide-open rules
- [x] CI: terraform fmt, validate, and basic unit tests
- [x] E2E apply in dev account and smoke validation
- [x] Review comments addressed

Upgrade/rollback notes:
- Module is additive by default. When enabling adoption of existing resources, operators must set adopt_existing = true and supply resource IDs to avoid replacement.
- Changing subnet CIDR or route tables will trigger replacements; the module docs include migration steps to add secondary subnets and shift traffic via routing changes to avoid downtime.

References: Linear ENG-4128 (control-plane networking), ENG-4210 (private installer integration). Related PRs: infra/terraform changes in previous PRs that added shared VPC references.

Implementation details (brief):
- VPC module creates: VPC, public/private subnets per-AZ, NAT gateway optional (configurable per-az), route tables, IGW, Egress-only IGW for IPv6 optional.
- Endpoints: aws_vpc_endpoint (interface) for ssm, ec2messages, ssmmessages, ecr.api; gateway endpoint for s3 when enabled.
- SGs: control_plane_sg (egress-only open for required addresses), management_sg (restricted to ops CIDRs), endpoint_sg (for interface endpoints).
- Peering: resource aws_vpc_peering_connection with acceptors and optional auto-accept module behavior; supports tags and name conventions used by the installer.

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to security_group rule defaults — I intentionally kept least privilege while enabling installer bootstrap flows.
- I added adopt_existing_* variables for safe migration; please review naming and UX.
- TGW/Transit support is intentionally opt-in; full Transit Gateway automation will be follow-up.

review_comments: Daniel Kim (reviewer): Can you tighten the management_sg inbound rules? Right now 0.0.0.0/0 is allowed for health checks — prefer explicit ops CIDRs or a parameter to opt-in.

Aisha Rahman (author): Fixed in commit 'feat(terraform): tighten management_sg and add ops_cidrs variable'. Management SG now defaults to empty and must be set by installer or LF ops. Added unit test for empty default.
Marta Gonzalez (reviewer): For peering, we need an option to accept peering from an existing connection created by the customer. Can we add a parameter to provide an existing_peering_id?

Aisha Rahman (author): Added 'existing_peering_id' variable and acceptance branch in peering logic; documented behavior in README. If provided, module will not create a new peering connection and will attempt to accept the provided id if auto_accept is true.
Liam O'Connell (reviewer): Route53 delegation looks good, but we need clear docs on cross-account delegation steps for enterprise customers.
Aisha Rahman (author): Expanded docs with a step-by-step delegation guide and example AWS CLI commands. Added migration notes for teams that already host private zones.
Marta Gonzalez (approval): Approving after changes look good. Please ensure CI is green before merge.
